t: The Treaty of Trianon of 1920 cost Hungary 72% of its historical territory and 58% of its population, and left more than three million ethnic Hungarians outside its borders.
Hungary was a kingdom without royalty: after the Diet dethroned Charles IV in 1921, Miklós Horthy ruled as regent until the Germans overthrew him in 1944.
As an Axis power Hungary regained Hungarian-majority lands, and in 1944 Hungarian authorities deported hundreds of thousands of Jews to Nazi concentration camps, where most of them died.
dyk: The prime minister Gyula Gömbös is said to have coined the word "axis" for the alliance he wanted with Germany and Italy, and the two countries used it for their Rome–Berlin axis.
ev: A coalition of right-wing forces restores the monarchy, and Miklós Horthy is chosen regent on 1 March
Hungary signs the Treaty of Trianon on 4 June, losing Transylvania, much of Upper Hungary and Vojvodina
Charles IV fails to retake the throne, and the Diet abolishes the House of Habsburg's rights to it
The First Vienna Award returns the southern parts of Czechoslovakia to Hungary
The Second Vienna Award assigns Northern Transylvania to Hungary
Hungary joins the invasion of Yugoslavia and, on 27 June, declares war on the Soviet Union
Germany occupies Hungary in March, and in October overthrows Horthy and installs Ferenc Szálasi of the Arrow Cross Party
The monarchy is formally abolished on 1 February and replaced by the Second Hungarian Republic

f.founder: A coalition of right-wing political forces, with Miklós Horthy chosen as regent on 1 March 1920
f.predecessor: The Hungarian Democratic Republic and the Hungarian Soviet Republic, after the dissolution of Austria-Hungary
f.successor: The Second Hungarian Republic (1946), followed by the Hungarian People's Republic (1949)
